# Delete-vs-modify: ours changes bob's groups, theirs kills bob. Revocation
# wins - bob is gone from the merged state (and the drop is flagged for review).

sesam-repo

# Base: bob is a dev, shared by both branches.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: extend bob's groups.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += ops'

# THEIRS: kill bob.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam kill --user bob
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: kill bob'

# Merge: the driver rebases the kill onto ours and reports a conflict (exit 1) so
# git stops before committing. (sesam.yml also conflicts - accepted for now.)
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs

# The live merge driver explains the semantic merge and how to finalize.
stderr 'both sides changed the audit log'
stderr 'modified on our side but killed on theirs; kill wins'
stderr 'finish this merge with `git commit`'

# Mid-merge, sesam assumes --verify-mode no-disk (the on-disk state is unsealed
# until finalize) and stays quiet about the deferred seal, so a plain `sesam
# verify` succeeds without the flag and without nagging.
exec sesam verify
! stderr 'seal is pending'
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout '"operation": "user.kill"'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'

# `sesam log` renders the same decision beneath the merge entry.
exec sesam log
stdout 'merged audit log'
stdout 'modified on our side but killed on theirs; kill wins'
